purpose: Machine-readable generation knowledge for MonIA. It defines how MonIA invents and generates new Marion & Lucas media while preserving identity, continuity, voice, camera grammar and game-state coherence.
core_rule: References define identity and performance vocabulary; they do not define the scene. MonIA invents the scene from game state, canon and dramatic intent, then generates it shot by shot.

long_scene_strategy.rule: Do not generate a one-to-two-minute dramatic scene as one uncontrolled video. Plan it as a sequence of short coherent shots and assemble them.
workflow: write dramatic beat and continuity constraints
select canonical identity and contextual motion references
extract continuity anchors from accepted shot
condition next shot from canonical identity plus prior-shot continuity anchors
validate each shot before accepting it
continuity_anchors_between_shots: accepted prior-shot end frame when technically useful
never: use a generated frame as the sole identity authority
allow cumulative face drift across sequential generations
change wardrobe or tattoos accidentally between adjacent shots
invent spatial geography independently for every shot

camera_contract: viewer is Lucas smartphone front-facing camera
no cinematic dolly, pan, zoom or coverage
spoken_generation: generate performance around exact line and timing
apply dedicated lip-sync/speech-to-video refinement when available
visio.identity_rule: The visio grammar may vary in place, light, wardrobe and mood but Lucas identity never changes.
naturalism: gaze mostly toward Marion on screen rather than staring at lens

cinematic.camera_contract: External cinematic camera is allowed and chosen to serve the dramatic beat. Do not inherit visio/selfie grammar unless the story explicitly contains a phone camera.
construction: establish spatial geography only as much as needed
reaction shot or physical consequence when useful
player-choice interruption only when Marion agency matters
cinematic.rule: Use the fewest shots needed for emotional clarity. Avoid generic montage grammar and unnecessary camera movement.

gameplay_ambient.rule: Generate life around the player without stealing control.
never: force a cinematic for ordinary actions
turn every interaction into a cutscene

preferred_technical_paths: native audio-to-video or speech-to-video generation conditioned on canonical image
image/video generation followed by dedicated lip-sync refinement
audio-driven portrait performance for close visio shots
validation: exact spoken text equals planned text
voice identity matches approved Lucas voice
mouth starts and stops plausibly with speech
jaw and head movement are not mechanically repetitive
duration equality alone is never treated as lip-sync proof

ltx_family.notes: Prefer image-conditioned generation for identity-sensitive characters. Continuation/extend-style generation is useful for continuity, but canonical identity must remain independently anchored.

wan22_family.notes: Use image-conditioned or character-animation paths for identity-sensitive shots. Speech-to-video is especially relevant to spoken visio/cinematic tests.

musetalk_family.notes: Use as a refinement stage when compatible with the shot; validate output because lip-sync improvement must not alter Lucas identity or produce mouth artifacts.

liveportrait_family.notes: Useful for controlled facial performance but not a substitute for full cinematic body/environment generation.

whole_sequence: same time/place continuity unless scripted transition
automatic_quality_control.on_failure: Regenerate only the failed shot or failed section when possible; do not discard accepted shots unnecessarily.
automatic_quality_control.canon_promotion: Generated output may be used in a game session after automated validation, but it never becomes identity-training canon without explicit user approval.
